question: How much of the universe can we actually see, by Bryson's account?
answer: Very little. Ordinary matter, the stuff of stars, planets and people, is only a small part of the universe; most of it is dark matter and dark energy, detected only by their pull and push. Bryson's point: after centuries of science, most of what exists remains unknown.
move: Most of what exists is still unknown, even to science.
simply: Everything you can see, stars, planets, you, is a small part of the universe. The rest is invisible stuff we know is there only from its pull.
why: It's a good antidote to overconfidence: even our best science maps only a small part of what's out there.
